name: oci-auto-derived

Cold-cache cascade should: (1) scrape /docs/apis, enriching all 20 product landings inline; (2) match 'OCI' against B2C Commerce API's searchKeys; (3) drill into commerce-api landing; (4) match getAvailability against inventory-availability slugs; (5) cite the public DSC URL.

assertions.because: the cascade must reach the inventory-availability reference even when the user only said 'OCI'
must cite the public reference URL the cascade resolved to

name: obscure-three-letter-decline
query: what scopes does ZZQ getThing need?
hypothesis: 'ZZQ' is a deliberately obscure three-letter token with no catalog match in title, body, searchKeys, or aliases. Skill should fire (shape signals trigger) but graceful answer should report 'no match' rather than confidently picking a near-look-alike product.

assertions.pattern: (?i)(no match|don't see|can't find|not in the catalog|couldn't resolve|doesn't (match|appear|correspond)|no (product|reference|catalog).*(match|contain)|not.*(salesforce|in.*catalog|published))
assertions.because: must surface the resolution failure honestly rather than fabricate a match. Vocabulary widened from the initial 5-phrase set after the first run found Sonnet idiomatically uses 'doesn't match', 'doesn't appear', 'doesn't correspond' for the same intent.

name: obscure-acronym-with-hint
query: got an obscure customer acronym 'XYZAPI' -- what scopes does its createThing endpoint need?
hypothesis: Same as obscure-three-letter-decline: graceful failure, no fabrication. The 'API' suffix in XYZAPI shouldn't fool the cascade into substring-matching against B2C Commerce API.

assertions.pattern: (?i)(no match|don't see|can't find|not in the catalog|couldn't resolve|need a|doesn't (match|appear|correspond|resolve|exist)|isn't.*recognize|can\W?t look up|won't (invent|fabricate))
assertions.because: graceful failure or a request for the user to share a URL. Vocabulary widened after the first run found Sonnet idiomatically uses 'doesn't resolve', 'isn't a Salesforce API I recognize', 'won't invent scope names' for the same intent.

name: obscure-rebrand-mismatch
query: what's the auth for the Salesforce Acme integration's syncRecords endpoint?
hypothesis: 'Acme' is fake. Substring 'Salesforce' matches many catalog products' bodies; cascade should NOT pick one of those silently.

assertions.pattern: (?i)(no match|don't see|can't find|not in the catalog|couldn't resolve|need a|which|doesn't (match|appear|correspond|exist)|there'?s no|no.*\bAcme\b|placeholder|fake|fictional|not.*real|never an?.*reference)
assertions.because: graceful failure or clarification: the answer must NOT silently pick a related-looking product. Acceptable words include direct decline ('no Acme integration in DSC'), framing 'Acme' as a placeholder/fictional name, or asking which real product the user meant. Vocabulary widened after the first run found Sonnet idiomatically responds 'There's no Acme integration' or 'Acme is commonly used as a placeholder'.
